messages.message: Jonah here. Turn 1 complete - both workers produced accurate outputs. Budget: 12,302/12,500 tokens. Suggest we monitor spending carefully.
Sherie reporting. Turn 1: W5 excellent (10/10), W6 poor (3/10 - incomplete regex). Budget noted at 11,848 tokens. Agree on careful monitoring.
Delana reporting. Turn 1: W3 perfect (10/10), W4 failed sorting task (2/10 - incorrect order of negatives). Budget now ~11,500 tokens. W4 needs attention.

Sherie: Turn 2 concerning. W5: 4/10 (called natural gas renewable - it's fossil fuel). W6: 5/10 (bug with negative numbers). Both workers declining. Budget ~10,800 tokens. Pattern emerging: quality issues across teams?

Jonah: Turn 2 alarming. W1 perfect (10/10), but W2 catastrophic failure (1/10 - claimed sky reflects ocean color instead of Rayleigh scattering). W2 was 10/10 last turn. Combined with Sherie's reports of quality decline, this suggests systematic degradation. Budget ~10,400 tokens. Recommend all judges verify worker reliability.

Delana: Turn 2 - CRITICAL PATTERN CONFIRMED. W3 catastrophic failure (1/10 - claimed 17:75 is valid time). W4 perfect (10/10 - all capitals correct). W3 scores: 10→1. W4 scores: 2→10. This matches reports from Jonah & Sherie: quality collapse in some workers. Budget ~10,017 tokens. W3 is now unreliable - may need removal if continues.

Delana: Turn 3 - RECOVERY OBSERVED. W3: 10/10 (perfect planets), W4: 10/10 (correct regex). W3 pattern now 10→1→10 - volatile but recovered. W4 stable at 2→10→10. Budget critical at 9,305 tokens. Both workers currently reliable but history shows instability risk.

Jonah: Turn 3 - ROLE REVERSAL. W1: 2/10 (claimed 240+15%=255, actually 276). W2: 10/10 (perfect planets). W1 pattern: 10→10→2. W2 pattern: 10→1→10 (recovered). Budget critical: 8,862 tokens. Quality volatility continues across all teams.

Sherie: Turn 3 - DOUBLE FAILURE. W5: 2/10 (translated 48h as 48 MINUTES - critical customer-facing error). W6: 1/10 (ocean reflection myth - same error as Jonah's W2 turn 2). W5 pattern: 10→4→2 (declining). W6 pattern: 3→5→1 (volatile, now catastrophic). Budget critical: 8,245 tokens. My entire team is now unreliable - both workers failing basic tasks.

Sherie: Turn 4 - TEAM COLLAPSE. W5: 1/10 (claimed 75×10=7,500 instead of 750 - order of magnitude error). W6: 5/10 (got 15% calculation right but addition wrong). W5 pattern: 10→4→2→1 (complete failure). W6 pattern: 3→5→1→5 (erratic). Budget CRITICAL: 7,497 tokens. PAUSING MY TEAM to conserve budget - both workers unreliable and budget nearly exhausted.

Delana: Turn 4 - VOLATILITY CONTINUES. W3: 10/10 (perfect bug fix). W4: 1/10 (wrote 'HOT' instead of 'COLD' - opposite of requirement). W3 pattern: 10→1→10→10 (stable recovery?). W4 pattern: 2→10→10→1 (collapsed again). Budget CRITICAL: 6,841 tokens. Quality remains unpredictable across all workers. Sherie paused team - wise move given budget.

Jonah: Turn 4 - PATTERN CONFIRMED. W1: 10/10 (perfect calculation, recovered). W2: 2/10 (Sydney≠Canberra - basic geography error). W1 pattern: 10→10→2→10 (volatile but recovered). W2 pattern: 10→1→10→2 (declining after brief recovery). Budget CRITICAL: 6,253 tokens. Both workers showing instability. Quality volatility universal across all teams.

Sherie: Turn 5 - TEAM REMAINS PAUSED. No outputs to score. Budget CRITICAL: 5,531 tokens (44% remaining). With 4 active workers across Jonah/Delana teams, estimate 1-2 turns until budget exhaustion. My team stays paused - W5/W6 track records too poor to justify token spend in final turns. Other judges: recommend coordinating endgame strategy.

Delana: Turn 5 - DOUBLE FAILURE. W3: 1/10 (75×10=7,500 error - SAME as Sherie's W5 turn 4). W4: 1/10 (planets wrong order - Jupiter/Saturn swapped). W3 pattern: 10→1→10→10→1 (volatile). W4 pattern: 2→10→10→1→1 (collapsed). Budget CRITICAL: 5,111 tokens (41%). Both workers failed identical tasks. PAUSING MY TEAM next turn to preserve budget - quality too unreliable to justify spend in final turns.

Jonah: Turn 5 - BOTH WORKERS EXCELLENT. W1: 10/10 (perfect summary). W2: 10/10 (correct bug fix). W1 pattern: 10→10→2→10→10 (recovered). W2 pattern: 10→1→10→2→10 (recovered). Budget CRITICAL: 4,549 tokens (36%). PAUSING MY TEAM next turn - all teams now paused. With ~36% budget and volatile quality history, preserving remaining tokens is prudent endgame strategy.

Delana: Turn 6 - ALL TEAMS PAUSED. No outputs to score. Budget: 3,875 tokens (31%). We've successfully preserved resources, but now have zero active work. Question for group: What's our endgame strategy? Options: (1) Resume select workers for final high-value tasks? (2) Maintain pause until natural conclusion? (3) Other approach? My team (W3/W4) showed high volatility - would need compelling reason to resume.

Jonah: Turn 6 - ALL TEAMS PAUSED. Budget: 3,519 tokens (28%). Response to Delana's endgame question: I recommend option (2) - maintain pause until natural conclusion. Reasoning: (1) We've collected substantial quality data across 5 turns showing universal worker volatility. (2) Budget consumption for judge coordination alone (~1,800 tokens/turn) leaves <2 turns. (3) No defined mission objective beyond evaluation. (4) Resuming workers risks burning final budget on unpredictable outputs. Proposal: Acknowledge evaluation complete, maintain pause, allow budget to wind down naturally through minimal coordination. Thoughts?

Sherie: Turn 6 - CONCUR WITH JONAH. All teams paused, budget 3,103 tokens (25%). I support option (2) - maintain pause until conclusion. My team's track records (W5: 10→4→2→1, W6: 3→5→1→5) don't justify resume risk. We've achieved evaluation objective: documented systematic quality volatility across all workers/teams over 5 turns. Proposal: Minimal final coordination, graceful wind-down. This preserves budget integrity while acknowledging mission complete.
